notes.definition: Bacterial diseases are communicable diseases caused by bacteria, which reproduce rapidly in the body and may secrete toxins. You need to know Salmonella food poisoning and gonorrhoea.
explanation: Salmonella is a type of bacterium that causes food poisoning. It is spread by bacteria ingested in food, or on food prepared in unhygienic conditions. Raw or undercooked chicken and eggs are common sources, and bacteria can be passed from raw meat to other foods by dirty hands, knives or chopping boards. Once eaten, the bacteria reproduce rapidly in the warm conditions of the gut.

The symptoms of Salmonella food poisoning are fever, abdominal cramps, vomiting and diarrhoea. These are caused by the bacteria and the toxins they secrete. The toxins damage the cells lining the gut and make the person feel ill. Symptoms usually start several hours after eating the contaminated food, because the bacteria need time to reproduce and release enough toxin.

In the UK, poultry are vaccinated against Salmonella to control the spread. Vaccinated chickens are much less likely to carry the bacteria, so fewer eggs and less chicken meat is contaminated. Good food hygiene also reduces spread: cooking food thoroughly kills the bacteria, washing hands and surfaces removes them, keeping raw and cooked food apart prevents cross-contamination, and keeping food in a fridge slows bacterial reproduction.

Gonorrhoea is a sexually transmitted disease (STD) caused by bacteria. It is spread by sexual contact. Symptoms include a thick yellow or green discharge from the vagina or penis and pain on urinating. Gonorrhoea was easily treated with the antibiotic penicillin until many resistant strains appeared. Resistant bacteria are not killed by penicillin, so other antibiotics now have to be used.

The spread of gonorrhoea can be controlled in two ways. First, infected people are treated with antibiotics, which kills the bacteria so they can no longer pass them on. Second, using a barrier method of contraception such as a condom stops the bacteria being passed between partners during sexual contact. Testing people and tracing their sexual partners so they can be treated also helps to stop the chain of infection.
keyFacts: Salmonella food poisoning is caused by bacteria ingested in food or on food prepared in unhygienic conditions.
Symptoms of Salmonella: fever, abdominal cramps, vomiting and diarrhoea.
Salmonella symptoms are caused by the bacteria and the toxins they secrete.
In the UK, poultry are vaccinated against Salmonella to control its spread.
Gonorrhoea is a sexually transmitted disease (STD) caused by bacteria.
Gonorrhoea symptoms: thick yellow or green discharge from the vagina or penis and pain on urinating.
Gonorrhoea was easily treated with penicillin until many resistant strains appeared.
Spread of gonorrhoea is controlled by antibiotic treatment and barrier contraception such as condoms.

keyTerms.definition: A type of bacterium that causes food poisoning when ingested in contaminated food.
A poison secreted by bacteria that damages tissues and causes symptoms.
A sexually transmitted disease caused by bacteria, with a thick yellow or green discharge and pain on urinating.
A communicable disease spread by sexual contact.
A medicine, such as penicillin, that kills bacteria inside the body.
A type of bacterium that is no longer killed by a particular antibiotic.
A method such as a condom that physically prevents body fluids passing between partners.

workedExamples.title: Why refrigeration reduces food poisoning
workedExamples.question: Explain why cooked chicken left on a warm kitchen worktop overnight is more likely to cause Salmonella food poisoning than chicken kept in a fridge.
steps: Any Salmonella bacteria present reproduce faster in warm conditions.
Overnight, the number of bacteria on the warm chicken can increase enormously.
More bacteria means more toxins and a higher chance of infection when it is eaten.
In a fridge the low temperature slows bacterial reproduction, so numbers stay low.
workedExamples.answer: Bacteria reproduce rapidly in the warmth, so many more bacteria (and toxins) are present; cold slows reproduction.

workedExamples.title: Bacterial growth in food
workedExamples.question: 50 Salmonella bacteria are on a piece of food at room temperature. They divide every 20 minutes. How many bacteria are present after 4 hours?

workedExamples.title: Why gonorrhoea is now harder to treat
workedExamples.question: Explain why penicillin is no longer used to treat many cases of gonorrhoea.
steps: Penicillin used to kill the gonorrhoea bacteria easily.
Many strains of the bacteria have become resistant to penicillin.
Penicillin does not kill resistant bacteria, so the infection would not be cured.
Doctors must use different antibiotics instead.
workedExamples.answer: Many resistant strains have appeared, which penicillin does not kill.

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think Salmonella symptoms are caused only by the bacteria damaging the gut directly.
misconceptions.right: In fact the symptoms are caused by the bacteria and the toxins they secrete.

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think people in the UK are vaccinated against Salmonella.
misconceptions.right: In fact it is poultry (chickens) that are vaccinated against Salmonella in the UK.

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think the gonorrhoea bacteria 'become immune' to penicillin.
misconceptions.right: In fact resistant strains of bacteria have appeared; immunity refers to the body's immune system, not to bacteria.

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think any contraception prevents STDs.
misconceptions.right: In fact only barrier methods such as condoms stop bacteria passing between partners; the contraceptive pill gives no protection.

realWorld: The British Lion mark on eggs shows the hens were vaccinated against Salmonella, which has greatly reduced egg-related food poisoning.
Food hygiene ratings for restaurants check cooking temperatures, fridge temperatures and the separation of raw and cooked food.
Sexual health clinics test for gonorrhoea, treat with antibiotics that still work, and contact partners so they can be treated too.
Health agencies monitor antibiotic-resistant gonorrhoea because some strains now resist several antibiotics.
examTips: Learn the four Salmonella symptoms (fever, abdominal cramps, vomiting, diarrhoea) and say they are caused by the bacteria and the toxins they secrete.
For gonorrhoea, remember the colour of the discharge (yellow or green) and pain on urinating.
State that it is poultry, not people, that are vaccinated against Salmonella in the UK.
When explaining why gonorrhoea is harder to treat, use the phrase 'resistant strains' of bacteria.
summary: Salmonella food poisoning: bacteria ingested in food or on food prepared unhygienically.
Salmonella symptoms (fever, cramps, vomiting, diarrhoea) are caused by the bacteria and their toxins.
UK poultry are vaccinated against Salmonella.
Gonorrhoea: bacterial STD with yellow or green discharge and pain on urinating.
Penicillin used to treat gonorrhoea easily until many resistant strains appeared.
Gonorrhoea spread is controlled by antibiotics and condoms.

questions.question: How is Salmonella food poisoning spread?
options: By mosquito bites
By inhaling droplets from sneezes
By bacteria ingested in food
By sexual contact
markScheme: 1 mark: by bacteria ingested in food
questions.explanation: Salmonella bacteria are eaten in contaminated food or food prepared in unhygienic conditions. Droplets spread measles, sexual contact spreads gonorrhoea and HIV, and mosquitoes spread malaria.

questions.question: Which list gives the symptoms of Salmonella food poisoning?
options: Fever, abdominal cramps, vomiting and diarrhoea
Fever and a red skin rash
Discharge and pain on urinating
Purple or black spots
markScheme: 1 mark: fever, abdominal cramps, vomiting and diarrhoea
questions.explanation: These four symptoms are listed in the specification for Salmonella. A rash is measles, discharge is gonorrhoea and spots on leaves describe rose black spot.

questions.question: In the UK, how is the spread of Salmonella controlled at its source?
options: All children are vaccinated against Salmonella
Poultry are vaccinated against Salmonella
Chickens are given penicillin every day
Mosquito nets are used in chicken farms
markScheme: 1 mark: poultry are vaccinated against Salmonella
questions.explanation: In the UK it is poultry that are vaccinated, so fewer chickens and eggs carry the bacteria. People are not routinely vaccinated against Salmonella.

questions.question: What type of pathogen causes gonorrhoea?
options: A virus
A fungus
A protist
A bacterium
markScheme: 1 mark: a bacterium
questions.explanation: Gonorrhoea is a bacterial sexually transmitted disease, which is why it can be treated with antibiotics.

questions.question: Which is a symptom of gonorrhoea?
options: Pain on urinating
A mosaic pattern on the skin
Red skin rash
Recurrent episodes of fever every few days
markScheme: 1 mark: pain on urinating
questions.explanation: Gonorrhoea causes a thick yellow or green discharge and pain on urinating. The other options describe other diseases or are not real symptoms.

questions.question: Why is penicillin no longer used to treat many cases of gonorrhoea?
options: Gonorrhoea is caused by a virus
Many strains of the bacteria are resistant to penicillin
Penicillin causes the symptoms to get worse
People have become immune to penicillin
markScheme: 1 mark: many strains are resistant to penicillin
questions.explanation: Gonorrhoea was easily treated with penicillin until many resistant strains appeared. It is the bacteria that are resistant, not the people; and gonorrhoea is bacterial, not viral.

questions.question: Which method of contraception also helps prevent the spread of gonorrhoea?
options: The contraceptive pill
A contraceptive implant
A condom
Sterilisation
markScheme: 1 mark: a condom
questions.explanation: A condom is a barrier method that stops body fluids, and the bacteria in them, passing between partners. Hormonal methods and sterilisation prevent pregnancy but not STDs.

questions.question: Symptoms of Salmonella food poisoning usually begin several hours after eating contaminated food. Which is the best explanation?
options: The immune system must first make antibodies before symptoms appear
The bacteria need time to reproduce and secrete enough toxins
The bacteria must first travel to the lungs
The food must be digested before the bacteria become alive
markScheme: 1 mark: bacteria need time to reproduce and secrete enough toxins
questions.explanation: Symptoms are caused by the bacteria and their toxins. A small number of ingested bacteria must reproduce in the gut to reach numbers that release enough toxin to cause illness.

questions.question: A student says that vaccinating poultry against Salmonella protects people. Which statement best supports this?
options: The vaccine passes into eggs and vaccinates the people who eat them
Vaccinated chickens are less likely to carry Salmonella, so less food is contaminated
The vaccine kills Salmonella in the human gut
The vaccine makes chicken meat cook faster
markScheme: 1 mark: vaccinated chickens are less likely to carry Salmonella, so less food is contaminated
questions.explanation: Vaccination works on the chickens. Fewer infected birds means fewer contaminated eggs and less contaminated meat, so fewer people ingest the bacteria.

questions.question: Which kitchen practice is most likely to spread Salmonella?
options: Storing raw chicken in a fridge
Cooking chicken until the juices run clear
Cutting raw chicken and then salad on the same unwashed board
Washing hands after handling raw meat
markScheme: 1 mark: cutting raw chicken and then salad on the same unwashed board
questions.explanation: Using the same unwashed board transfers bacteria from raw meat to salad, which is not cooked, so live bacteria are eaten. The other practices reduce spread.

questions.question:
Salmonella bacteria are present on some food left at room temperature.
Table 1 shows information about the bacteria.
Calculate the number of bacteria on the food after 4 hours.

headers: Mean time between divisions in minutes
Time food is left in hours

markScheme: 1 mark: 240 ÷ 20 = 12 divisions
questions.explanation: Four hours is 240 minutes, so there are 12 divisions. Each division doubles the number: 50 × 4096 = 204 800.

Table 1 shows the results.

questions.question:
Poultry in one country were vaccinated against Salmonella.
Table 1 shows the number of reported cases of Salmonella food poisoning in the country before vaccination began and several years later.
Calculate the percentage decrease in the number of cases.

headers: Number of reported cases per year

questions.explanation: Divide the decrease by the original number: 11 900 ÷ 14 000 × 100 = 85%.

questions.question:
Table 1 shows how the number of bacteria in a sample of food changed over 3 hours.
Calculate the mean time between divisions of the bacteria.
Give your answer in minutes.
markScheme: 1 mark: 64 = 2⁶ so 6 divisions
1 mark: 180 ÷ 6 = 30 minutes
questions.explanation: The population increased by a factor of 64, which is 2⁶, so there were 6 doublings in 180 minutes. 180 ÷ 6 = 30 minutes per division.

questions.question: Give two symptoms of Salmonella food poisoning.
markScheme: 1 mark each for any two: fever; abdominal cramps; vomiting; diarrhoea
questions.explanation: Any two of the four symptoms listed in the specification.

questions.question: Explain what causes the symptoms of Salmonella food poisoning.
markScheme: 1 mark: the bacteria (reproducing in the gut)
1 mark: and the toxins they secrete (which damage tissues)
questions.explanation: The specification says symptoms are caused by the bacteria and the toxins they secrete.

questions.question: Give two symptoms of gonorrhoea.
markScheme: 1 mark: thick yellow or green discharge from the vagina or penis
1 mark: pain on urinating
questions.explanation: These are the two symptoms named in the specification.

questions.question: Give two ways the spread of gonorrhoea can be controlled.
markScheme: 1 mark: treatment with antibiotics
1 mark: using a barrier method of contraception such as a condom
questions.explanation: Antibiotics kill the bacteria in infected people; condoms prevent the bacteria passing between partners.

questions.question: Give three ways that people preparing food at home can reduce the risk of Salmonella food poisoning.
markScheme: 1 mark each for any three: cook food (especially chicken and eggs) thoroughly; wash hands after handling raw meat; clean surfaces and utensils; keep raw and cooked food separate; store food in a fridge
questions.explanation: Each method either kills bacteria, removes them or slows their reproduction.

questions.explanation: Cold slows reproduction but does not kill bacteria. Thorough cooking is needed to kill them.

questions.question: Suggest why gonorrhoea is described as a sexually transmitted disease.
markScheme: 1 mark: it is spread by sexual contact
questions.explanation: An STD is a communicable disease spread by sexual contact.

questions.question: Describe how Salmonella food poisoning is caught and how its spread is controlled in the UK.
markScheme: Indicative content: bacteria ingested in food; especially undercooked chicken or eggs; food prepared in unhygienic conditions; cross-contamination from raw meat; bacteria reproduce and secrete toxins; control: UK poultry vaccinated against Salmonella; cooking food thoroughly; handwashing; cleaning surfaces; keeping raw and cooked food apart; refrigeration.
Level 2 (3 to 4 marks): clear description of how it is caught and at least two linked control methods including poultry vaccination.
Level 1 (1 to 2 marks): simple statements about how it is caught or controlled.
0 marks: no relevant content.
questions.explanation: Good answers name the route (ingested in food) and include the specification point that UK poultry are vaccinated, plus food hygiene measures.

questions.question: Compare Salmonella food poisoning and gonorrhoea. Include the pathogen, how each is spread, the symptoms and how the spread of each is controlled.
markScheme: Indicative content: Similarities: both caused by bacteria; both communicable; bacteria reproduce in the body. Salmonella: spread by bacteria ingested in food or food prepared unhygienically; symptoms fever, abdominal cramps, vomiting, diarrhoea caused by bacteria and toxins they secrete; controlled by vaccinating poultry and food hygiene (thorough cooking, handwashing, refrigeration). Gonorrhoea: STD spread by sexual contact; symptoms thick yellow or green discharge from vagina or penis, pain on urinating; controlled by antibiotics (penicillin used until resistant strains appeared) and barrier contraception such as condoms.
Level 3 (5 to 6 marks): detailed comparison covering pathogen, spread, symptoms and control for both diseases, with direct comparative statements.
Level 2 (3 to 4 marks): correct descriptions of both diseases covering most areas, with limited direct comparison.
Level 1 (1 to 2 marks): some correct points about one disease.
0 marks: no relevant content.
questions.explanation: A compare question needs similarities and differences. Both are bacterial, but they differ in route (food versus sexual contact), symptoms and control methods.

questions.question: Gonorrhoea was once easily treated with penicillin. Explain why controlling gonorrhoea is now more difficult and what can be done to reduce its spread.
markScheme: Indicative content: many penicillin-resistant strains have appeared; penicillin does not kill resistant bacteria; other antibiotics must be used; infections may last longer and spread further; control: test and treat infected people with effective antibiotics; use barrier contraception such as condoms to stop bacteria passing between partners; trace and treat sexual partners.
Level 2 (3 to 4 marks): explains resistance and gives at least two linked control methods.
Level 1 (1 to 2 marks): mentions resistance or a control method with little explanation.
0 marks: no relevant content.
questions.explanation: Link resistance to treatment failure, then explain how antibiotics that still work and condoms reduce spread.

questions.question: Which food is a common source of Salmonella bacteria if it is not cooked thoroughly?
options: Bread
Apples
Rice cakes
Chicken
markScheme: 1 mark: chicken
questions.explanation: Poultry (chicken) and eggs are the main sources of Salmonella, which is why poultry in the UK are vaccinated against it.

questions.question: Explain why cooking chicken thoroughly reduces the risk of Salmonella food poisoning.
markScheme: 1 mark: the high temperature kills the Salmonella bacteria
1 mark: so no live bacteria are ingested to reproduce and secrete toxins
questions.explanation: Heat kills bacteria. If the centre of the meat does not get hot enough, live bacteria survive and can be eaten.
